title: tpm2-tools slice 3 owes: a timed-out tool must let the CLI exit (#301 round 2 new 4)
description: After a tool_timeout the runTool pipe reads and child.exited stay pending, src/cli/ward.ts exits explicitly only when a provider reports abandonedCall, and only the direct child is killed (a grandchild is orphaned). Slice 3 at the latest: the TPM2 KeyProvider reports a timed-out tool through abandonedCall so the CLI exits explicitly, or runTool cancels its readers and unrefs the child on timeout; and if Bun supports it, spawn the tool in its own process group and kill the group.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A command whose tpm2 tool timed out exits after writing its output instead of waiting for a pipe or a stuck child, shown by a test
A tool spawned by the adapter and its grandchildren are killed together on timeout, or the task records why Bun cannot

implementationNotes: 3d-1a, 2026-11-15T02:40:34Z: probed Bun 1.3.14 on darwin: Bun.spawn detached:true puts the child in its own process group (child pgid == pid, grandchild shares it) and process.kill(-pid, 9) kills the grandchild. spawnTool now sets detached:true and runTool kills the group (fallback: the child alone). Tests: 'a timed-out tool's grandchild is killed with it' and 'a timed-out tool lets the process exit' (a probe that times a grandchild-holding tool out and never calls process.exit). The provider also reports abandonedCall() after a tool_timeout, so the CLI's explicit exit is a second mitigation. Linux behaviour of detached is NOT yet measured here (CI runs the tests on linux arm64); the real-output half of WCLI-157 is untouched.

2026-11-15T02:51:27Z #338 landed (squash 8bb9817), approved by ward-cli-review-338 (Opus). AC0 STAYS OPEN: #338 proves runTool, not a ward command, so it does not close AC0. AC1 is evidenced by 'a timed-out tool's grandchild is killed with it' (not ticked here; the leader decides). MEASURED 2026-11-15T02:51Z, alone: the grandchild-hang fake STAYS ALIVE until killed (fake alive at +0.5s, +1.5s, +2.5s and +4.0s after spawn, exitCode null; grandchild alive; one group kill ended both), so both tests exercise 'tool alive at timeout', not the post-reap path. RESIDUALS, named and not fixed: (1) detached puts the tool in its own session, out of the terminal's foreground group, so Ctrl-C or SIGHUP on ward orphans a running tpm2 tool; follow-up is a SIGINT/SIGTERM handler that kills live tool groups. (2) The PID-reuse window on an empty group is negligible. Do NOT add an exitCode guard: it would skip the grandchild kill.
